original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Answer #3443's open question for present-head flag 9 (X4 -> Y23, basis head 196): price changed schedules that co-host the head at Y23's delivering update (3124, the only Y23 update carrying X4) while X4 spans the head and is still live. Build two explicit splices of the published #1991 word, run the published p104-native-channel validate() on each with six newly lowered native edges, and give the exact before/after bill (events, ADDs, transport occurrences, rank mass, paid H_r profile, native edges, per-register surcharge). Add the same-class zero-mass obstruction in two least-frame models: with the private register C relaxed (as in #3532) and with C pinned to its published events (both repairs keep C unchanged). Report the rank-mass floor.
scope_change_reason: #3443 shows the published word hosts flag 9's head on Y23 only at its terminal transport and leaves pricing a repair open; #3508 priced flag 43 at zero added mass and #3532 priced flag 1 at +2 with 247 relocation slots left open. This package cites #3443 without reprinting its drop/arrive chronology, reuses the #3508/#3532 method through a flag-agnostic helper, and adds a private-pinned least-frame model that closes the relocation window for flag 9.
bottleneck_link: Flag 9 follows flag 1, not flag 43: every co-hosting repair in the order-preserving class and in the relocation class with C's events kept needs at least two added rank units, and two natively validated repairs reach exactly that floor (R0 order-preserving +1 event/+1 transport/+2 rank on D28; R1 relocated into D28's full window, 0 events/0 transports/+2 rank on Y23). With C relaxed, 173 late relocation slots stay relaxed-feasible, so the floor is closed only for the C-pinned class. This does not supply I-G/2, a side correction or a supplier.
stop_rule: Stop after one flag (9): one order-preserving repair R0 and one relocation R1, both natively validated and billed, plus the head closure and both exact least-frame zero-mass sweeps for every Y23 update and every relocation slot of the delivering ADD. Do not touch flags 0, 1 or 43, recompute relay coefficients beyond the X4 entry delivered into Y23, price I-G/2 or build a side correction.
evidence: Only 3124 (Y23 += D28/4, chart [447,127,192]) carries X4 into Y23 (-1/2, its final coefficient); D28's row is written only at 2520 and 3635 and Y23 is never read. X4 spans 196 at all nine Y23 updates (the event-500 drop in #3443 is generator-only). R0 retargets 3122 (D28 [447,192]->[447,127,192,196], rank 2), 3123 (Y23 [447,127]->[447,127,192,196], rank 2), relabels the 3124 chart to rank 4, inserts D28 [447,127,192,196]->[447,127,192] (rank 1) after it, and retargets 3489 (Y23 -> final, rank 4). R1 moves Y23's 3123/3124/3489 into D28's full window after 3634: Y23 [447,127]->FULL (rank 7), the ADD in FULL, Y23 FULL->final (rank 1). The published check_native.validate() passes on both (742 and 741 native edges, 208 adapters, 280 framed rows, 72 dirty helpers restored); independent replay gives 280/280 rows equal. Bill: R0 4059 events, 2624 ADDs, 1411 transports, rank mass 2370, profile delta -H1+2H2+H4-H5, +2 on D28; R1 4058 events, 2624 ADDs, 1410 transports, rank mass 2370, delta H7-H5, +2 on Y23; C untouched. X4 has five later reads after the delivering update in both words. Obstruction: all 280 non-private registers sit at their rank floor; the #3508 head closure blocks all nine Y23 updates (first Y24 or Y28; 5 obstructions at 3124); the least-frame sweep is infeasible for all nine order-preserving updates in both models; relocation (1114 slots in D28's window) is obstructed at 941 slots with C relaxed (feasible after Y103's read at 3462) and at all 1114 with C pinned, where D28's least frame after 3462 is forced to rank 6 by C's chart at 2520 and leaves final(Y23). Selected kappa unchanged.

open_questions.question: Does a zero-added-mass co-hosting relocation of flag 9's delivering ADD after 3462 exist once the private register C may change its charts?
open_questions.why_it_matters: With C pinned the +2 floor is closed over all 1114 slots; with C relaxed 173 late slots stay feasible. A construction would need to re-chart C (paying C's own mass), so it would test whether the relaxed sweep is ever realizable.
open_questions.first_step: Bound C's mass change needed to lower D27/D28's 2520 private chart [383] and the downstream Y103/Y31/Y22 least frames inside final(Y23); compare against the +2 non-private surcharge.
open_questions.blocked_by: The relaxed least solution leaves D28 empty at its reads, which conflicts with the published C chart [383]; no C re-charting is attempted here.

open_questions.question: Does the private-pinned least-frame sweep also close flag 1's 247 late relocation slots (#3532 open question 1)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would make the +2 floor relocation-global for flag 1 in the class that both #3532 repairs belong to, without a construction search.
open_questions.first_step: Load headstep.py by path with flag 1's constants (target Y7, head 232, delivery 2797) and run relocation_scan with Least(witness, pinned=True) in a separate package citing #3532.
open_questions.blocked_by: #3532 is a leave-alone prior here; flag 1 is not recomputed in this package.

open_questions.question: Which +2 repair is cheaper under the repository's actual per-rank weights?
open_questions.why_it_matters: R0 costs a+2b and R1 costs 2b under affine prices; R0's delta -H1+2H2+H4-H5 is +2 at H=r and -2 at H=r^2, so its sign depends on convexity, while R1's H7-H5 is nonnegative for any nondecreasing H.
open_questions.first_step: Evaluate both deltas under the per-rank weights used by the selected channel bill.
